forecasts.question: Will Hezbollah's official channels claim a publicly-acknowledged strike operation targeting Israeli forces or Israeli territory, confirmed by IDF or TIER1, before EOD 2026-08-26?
forecasts.delta_reason: New NEAR-TERM forecast. Hezbollah vowed an 'appropriate response' to Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon on August 15 that killed 11 people, including Badr unit commander Abu Hassan Alaa (France 24, August 15, 2026). As of August 23 — eight days elapsed — no publicly-claimed retaliatory strike has been confirmed by IDF or TIER1 sources (JPost liveblog August 21; Times of Israel August 22). Historical Hezbollah retaliation pattern: official operations typically claimed within 1-10 days of a named provocation, or after extended multi-week operational preparation. Eight days elapsed without execution reduces the 72-hour probability below the initial threat-week estimate, but the threat window remains live. p=0.22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hezbollah's official channel (Al-Manar TV, official Hezbollah Telegram or @Moqawama, or a named Hezbollah Secretary-General statement) claims a named strike operation targeting Israeli forces or Israeli territory, and this claim is independently confirmed by at least one IDF spokesperson statement or one TIER1 report (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera), between 2026-08-23 and EOD 2026-08-26.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hezbollah official claim PLUS one confirming IDF spokesperson statement OR one TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera/CNN) report of the same attack. Hezbollah claim without IDF or TIER1 confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An attack occurring without Hezbollah's official public claim on their named channels = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A TIER1 report of rocket fire attributed to Hezbollah without a Hezbollah official claim = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Attacks on Lebanese territory, Syrian territory, or non-Israeli/non-Israeli-linked targets are out of scope.

indicators.name: Al-Manar TV or official Hezbollah Telegram publishes a named claim of a strike on Israeli territory or Israeli forces
IDF Spokesperson confirms inbound fire attributed to Hezbollah (drones, rockets, or missiles from Lebanon into Israel)

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-09-04?
forecasts.delta_reason: Downward update from 0.25. The MOU framework expired 2026-08-17 without a successor. On 2026-08-22, US President Trump stated publicly that Iran 'was not ready for the right deal' and that Washington was 'observing what happens' — the most recent named-official characterization, with no upcoming meeting or mediator deployment cited (Al Jazeera live updates, August 22). No Omani, Qatari, or Swiss mediator published a readout in the 48-hour window surrounding or following MOU expiry. Iran parliament speaker Ghalibaf's August 22 reference to 'messages from neighboring nations' is a standard diplomatic-public formulation used before both engagements and confrontations; without a specific mediator readout, it is insufficient to move p upward. 12 days remain to the September 4 horizon, but the prerequisites — US withdrawal of the compensation demand and active mediator re-engagement — are not evidenced. Sunday cold-start audit: p_cold=0.10 (base rate of any formal session in a 14-day window given MOU collapse and no active mediator); gap vs p_inherited=0.25 is 15pp, exceeding the 7pp threshold. Judge selects 0.12 (evidence-based, slightly above pure cold rate of 0.10 to account for residual uncertainty).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals or envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman, Qatar, Switzerland, or Pakistan), between 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-04.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/CNBC/Al Jazeera; State Dept or Iran MFA statement naming a convened session also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Relay of written messages or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Secret back-channel meetings without principal confirmation from both sides = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Omani, Qatari, or Swiss mediator publishes a readout of a scheduled or held US-Iran session
Iranian MFA statement confirming re-engagement or lifting the compensation-demand precondition

forecasts.question: Will the Strait of Hormuz 7-day average commercial transit count reach or exceed 30 vessels per day before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. Lloyd's List Intelligence Strait of Hormuz Brief (August 19) recorded 73 commercial transits in the preceding 7 days, an average of 10.4 vessels per day against a pre-conflict baseline of approximately 130 per day. US News (August 20) confirms transits 'hover in single digits' for oil tankers specifically. Al Jazeera (August 20) notes dark-fleet contacts surpassed AIS-visible traffic for the first time. CNN (August 21) reports US gasoline prices up nearly one dollar year-over-year with Hormuz traffic 'remains low.' No P&I war-risk insurer re-entry announcement found in the 48-hour window. Trajectory unchanged.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Lloyd's List Intelligence, IMF PortWatch, or UNCTAD Maritime records a 7-day average commercial transit count of 30 or more vessels per day for any consecutive 7-day window ending on or before EOD 2026-09-07.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence (primary) OR IMF PortWatch data release OR Reuters or Bloomberg citing a named maritime tracking source. PGSA self-reported counts excluded unless confirmed by two or more independent AIS trackers.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Dark-fleet or unidentified vessels without AIS confirmation from a named tracker do NOT count toward the 30-per-day threshold. Naval escort vessels do NOT count as commercial transits. If primary trackers conflict by more than 30 percent, flag AMBIGUOUS.

indicators.name: Lloyd's List or PortWatch records 7-day Hormuz average rising above 20 vessels per day
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES — upward trajectory required as intermediate signal

indicators.name: P&I war-risk insurers announce any Hormuz transit coverage reinstatement for commercial vessels

forecasts.question: Will IRGC-attributed or Hezbollah forces conduct a publicly confirmed strike operation causing 10 or more casualties on Israeli or US-linked targets before EOD 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. Hezbollah's publicly-announced retaliation threat for the August 15 Israeli Lebanon strikes (11 killed, including Badr unit commander Abu Hassan Alaa; France 24, August 15) remains unexecuted through August 23 — eight days elapsed. Times of Israel liveblog (August 22) and JPost (August 21) contain no confirmed qualifying strike. IRGC General Staff, via Tasnim (August 23), warned weapons would be 'completely different from the past in every respect' — asserting readiness but not announcing an operation. CNN (August 20) reported new US Hezbollah financial sanctions, adding counter-deterrence. The MOU's informal halt-strikes compact (Axios, June 28) remains in undefined status post-MOU expiry August 17 — neither side has confirmed extension or dissolution. The non-execution signal (8 days, no qualifying strike) and the compact-uncertainty signal (MOU expired, compact undefined) roughly balance. p=0.38 held.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if two independent TIER1 sources (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) report a strike attributed to IRGC, IRGC-affiliated militia, or Hezbollah causing 10 or more confirmed casualties on Israeli military or civilian targets or US-linked targets (base, vessel, or personnel), between 2026-08-21 and 2026-09-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 sources OR one TIER1 plus an official Israeli IDF or US CENTCOM statement attributing the attack to IRGC or Hezbollah with a named casualty count.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Attribution to 'unknown militants' without IRGC or Hezbollah claim confirmed by IDF or CENTCOM = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Attacks on non-Israeli and non-US targets (e.g., Gulf Arab states only) = out of scope. Confirmed casualty count below 10 = NO.

indicators.name: IDF or CENTCOM statement attributing a strike to IRGC or Hezbollah with named casualties
Hezbollah or IRGC official channel claiming a named strike operation on Israeli or US targets

forecasts.question: Will Israeli authorities officially announce a postponement or cancellation of the Knesset election currently scheduled for October 27, 2026, before EOD 2026-09-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The Knesset dissolution bill's final reading, passed in July 2026 (Israel Hayom, July 12), set the election for October 27, the standard statutory date. Netanyahu's coalition fell below 61 seats in July 2026 (JPost/ToI), placing him in caretaker PM status through the October 27 election. The 2026 Iran war, ongoing Lebanon operations, and the post-MOU diplomatic vacuum create a non-trivial security-based postponement tail: caretaker governments have historically been reluctant to postpone elections without a security-critical necessity, and Israeli law and precedent strongly favor proceeding. The Board of Peace external advisory role (Times of Israel, August 19) has not publicly called for postponement. The 35-day window allows one security escalation cycle before the September 27 decision horizon. p=0.12 captures the security-risk tail without overstating it.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Israeli Central Elections Committee (CEA) or the Israeli government publishes an official notice in the Israel Official Gazette (Reshumot) postponing or cancelling the October 27, 2026 Knesset election, before EOD 2026-09-27.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israel Official Gazette (Reshumot) OR Reuters/AP/Times of Israel citing a named CEA Director or Israeli Supreme Court ruling ordering postponement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A postponement announced after September 27 does not resolve this forecast YES. A partial delay (only specific constituencies postponed) = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Security concerns cited by politicians without an official CEA or court order = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Israeli Supreme Court accepts a petition challenging the election schedule on security grounds
CEA official announcement of a revised election date published in Reshumot

forecasts.question: Will Iran formally agree, in a signed or jointly-confirmed written document, to cap uranium enrichment at or below 20 percent before EOD 2026-10-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Downward update from 0.18. The June 17-August 17 MOU expired without a successor framework addressing enrichment. The IAEA remains blocked from visiting Iranian enrichment sites as of the most recent reporting (IAEA GOV/2026/8 status; no new access announcement found in 48h). Iran's public posture — IRGC weapons-escalation rhetoric (Tasnim, August 23) and Pezeshkian defending the expired MOU against domestic hardliner criticism (Tehran Times, August 23) — does not reflect a government pursuing a new signed enrichment agreement. Trump's August 22 statement ('not ready for the right deal') eliminates the US-side diplomatic impetus. A signed enrichment cap before October 15 requires resumed talks (F2, p=0.12), compensation-demand resolution, and document execution — a sequence requiring at minimum 4-6 weeks in best case, against a 53-day horizon. Sunday cold-start audit: p_cold=0.06 (base rate given MOU collapse, no active talks, IAEA access blocked); gap vs p_inherited=0.18 is 12pp, exceeding 7pp threshold. Judge selects 0.08 (evidence-based; slight residual above cold floor 0.06 accounting for unconfirmed CBS Vance inspections-adjacent report).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the IAEA Director General or named US and Iranian officials confirm in a public statement that Iran has agreed to cap uranium enrichment at or below 20 percent, AND this is formalized in a signed joint document or jointly-acknowledged framework, between 2026-08-21 and 2026-10-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA Director General public statement OR Reuters/AP/AFP citing both a named US official and a named Iranian official confirming the enrichment cap commitment AND referencing a signed or formally-acknowledged document.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Verbal statements of 'willingness' or 'intent' without a signed document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. An agreed cap above 20 percent (e.g., at 60 percent) = NO. A cap applying only to specific declared facilities without a national commitment = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IAEA Director General public statement citing Iranian agreement on an enrichment ceiling at or below 20 percent
Iran MFA or Atomic Energy Organization formal announcement of enrichment suspension above 20 percent
